synopsis: The glossary identifies Sim2Radar, alongside RadSimReal, as a research tool addressing the radar simulation-to-reality gap [f15953]. In February 2026, Sim2Radar mapped materials to ITU-R P.2040-4 values at 77 GHz using a Fresnel ray tracer in Mitsuba 3 across five indoor scenes [f3931]. Simulated radar produced about 12% of real point density—251 versus 2,057 points per frame on average—with the passage attributing the gap to real radar’s diffuse scattering and higher-order multipath [f3932, f4305]. Chapter 5 also cites Sim2Radar as independent evidence for requiring wavelength- and band-specific lidar and radar material properties; the reported evaluation scope is five indoor scenes [f4298, f3931].

relations.note: Both report simulated radar reaching about 12% of real indoor point density.
Measured point-density shortfall demonstrates the simulation-to-reality radar gap described in the glossary.
